name: liked_palettes
title: What the admins liked
description: The admins' liked palettes, newest first: every admin's likes together, the site's standard of taste. Every palette in it looks good. `from` says where its latest like was pressed, when that was recorded: a palette liked from a search or a collection is a good answer to it. `in` lists the Grabient collections that hold it now.

collection.description: Only palettes liked from this collection or held by it.

search.description: Only palettes liked from this search.

recorded.description: Only likes whose search or collection was recorded.

name: curation_record
title: What the admins took out
description: The admins' record, newest first: palettes removed from a collection, deleted, redrawn or edited, with the reasons given. What was taken out, and why, is the other half of the site's taste. A palette removed or deleted never comes back.

seed.description: A palette seed, as in its address: k and 8 to 49 more characters.

name: palette_standing
title: Where palettes stand
description: For each palette: its place in the gallery, who liked it, the Grabient collections that hold it, its title, its reviews, and whether an admin took it out before. `locked` means a person liked it (an admin, a reader, or readers of grabient.com): it cannot be edited, redrawn or deleted.

items.description: A palette seed, as in its address: k and 8 to 49 more characters.

name: site_collections
title: Grabient's collections
description: The public collections Grabient made, with how many of each one's palettes an admin liked, how many have a review, and how many readers saved a copy (`saves`). `order` is updated (latest change first), title, or unreviewed (most palettes without a review first).

query.description: Words in the title, description or tags.

name: site_collection
title: One of Grabient's collections
description: A Grabient collection in full: its words, the admins' notes on it, and every palette in order with its likes, its title, whether an admin liked it (it fits and stays), whether it is locked, readers' fit votes and its reviews.

name: search_demand
title: What people search for
description: The searches people make most, most searched first: a year of grabient.com's searches with the last four weeks on this site added, connected apps' searches among them. `unread` is the last four weeks' searches in words the site can't read, that 3 searches or more made.

name: search_tags
title: The tags under the search
description: The searches every reader sees as tags under the search field, in the order they stand: the ones scheduled here, then up to four searches rising this week, then the most searched, and none says again what one before it says. With no `add` or `remove` it only reads: the row as it stands now, what is scheduled and what is rising, with its counts. `add` schedules searches to lead the row from a day to a day, in the order sent, up to 400 days ahead. `remove` takes scheduled ones out by id or by their batch's label. A tag is a search the site answers from its own vocabulary, so every tag finds palettes: other words are refused, with the nearest searches that would stand.

words.description: The search, as a reader would type it.

from.description: The day it starts (2026-10-20) or a moment (ISO 8601). Left out, now.

until.description: The last day it stands. Left out, 7 days from its start. At most 120 days.

label.description: A name for this batch, to find or remove it.

name: palette_use
title: How readers use the palettes
description: What readers did with the public palettes in the last days, counted with no address, account or cookie: with a collection, its page's views, each of its palettes' opens and copies by place, and how readers changed its palettes in the editor before taking them; without, the palettes taken most, the collections seen most and the editor's changes. The raw counts: visitor_signals weighs them by place. Readers' use says what is useful, not what is good: the admins' likes and record stand above it.

collection.description: A public collection's slug; left out, the whole site.

name: signups
title: Who signs up, and from where
description: Accounts made in the last weeks, week by week, and how each one's first visit reached Grabient: the campaign tags on the link, the site that sent it and the page it landed on. Those were saved only while the site's analytics ran, for a reader with analytics on, until October 2026: an account without them came with analytics off, straight to the site, or since; where readers come from is in site_visits now. Counts alone: no account, name or email. The seeding personas are left out, and admins are counted apart.

limit.description: How many of each kind of source, default 20.

annotations.title: Who signs up, and from where

name: visitor_signals
title: What readers use and pass over
description: What readers' use says about the collections, weighed by each palette's place on its page (a palette near the top is used more for being there): with a collection, each of its palettes' uses against what its place would earn (lift above 1 is more), the ones readers pass over and the ones they take, the styles they switch to and how they change its palettes in the editor; without, the collections seen most and taken least, every collection's passed-over and taken palettes, the searches answered badly or by no collection, and the site's style and editor changes. A collection needs `minUses` uses on its page to be judged. Counted with no address, account or cookie. It ranks below the admins' notes, record and likes in choosing what to make, extend or replace: it never earns a like, and a palette a person liked stays.

collection.description: A public collection's slug; left out, the whole site.

minUses.description: Uses on a collection's own page before it is judged, default 10.

limit.description: How many of each list, default 20.

annotations.title: What readers use and pass over

name: search_use
title: How well searches are answered
description: The searches readers made with Enter in the last days, in the words the site knows, with how many went on to open, copy or download a palette from the results: each search's count, uses and rate against the site's own, whether it is answered badly (5 searches or more, used at under half the site's rate) and whether a public collection has its words as its title. `unread` is the words the site can't read that 3 searches or more made, by page (mcp is connected apps' searches); `votes` is the thumbs signed-in readers gave the palettes a search showed. With `words`, the searches that hold them. Counted with no address, account or cookie. search_demand ranks what people search for; this says whether they found it.

words.description: Words a search holds; left out, every search.

name: site_usage
title: What the site's own work came to
description: The counts of the site's own work in the last days, from Workers Analytics Engine: MCP tool calls by server, tool, outcome, address and app, and the requests without a valid token; apps signing in, by step and outcome, with the authorization server's errors; requests a limit refused, by limit, with the site-wide ceilings that ran out; old grabient.com addresses by how they resolved; pictures drawn, served from the cache or refused; errors pages reported, by kind of page and browser; palette files fetched, by format and by who asked (this site, another site, or no page); answers that failed, by status and kind of address; and visits sent on to Google Analytics, by what they were, country, browser and network. Each day's totals too. This deploy's own counts. Nothing in them names a person.

limit.description: How many rows of each event, default 25.

annotations.title: What the site's own work came to

name: site_visits
title: Who visits the site
description: Visits counted by the site's own server from the pages browsers load, in the last days: each day's visitors, landings and pages loaded, and the share who used a palette, a collection or the search, about a third when only people are counted; of the visitors, the people, whose day showed a person (a landing from another site or a campaign link, a page loaded within the site or in a partner's frame, or something used or searched), and the unconfirmed rest, a landing from nowhere and nothing after it (Google Analytics instead receives every visitor whose browser ran a page, a landing from nowhere too; site_usage counts what it was sent); people's pages by kind of page, language, country, device, browser and system; their landings by page, the site that sent them and campaign tags; what was left out as programs (signals no browser sends, browser versions far behind, hosting networks, the unconfirmed); and the countries and networks whose visitors use palettes far less than the site's. A visitor is a code made with a key deleted when its day ends, so a reader on two days is two visitor-days. Nothing in them names a person.

limit.description: How many rows of each list, default 20.

name: credit_remove
title: Take a name off palettes
description: Take a reader's username off the palettes they liked first, at once and for good: the account cannot show that name there again, though a new username it takes is checked as any is. `restore` lets it show the name again once it turns the switch back on. An admin's name is the site's own.

username.description: The reader's username, in any case.

restore.description: Let the account show the name again.

name: palette_replace
title: Edit a palette
description: Put an edited palette in the place of one the site made: in the gallery and in every Grabient collection that holds it, with its date, its title and its scheduled likes. `to` is the edited palette's seed, as compose_palette or adjust_palette gives one. Refused for a locked palette. A person's own collections are never touched.

from.description: A palette seed, as in its address: k and 8 to 49 more characters.

to.description: A palette seed, as in its address: k and 8 to 49 more characters.

reasons.description: What is wrong with it. muddy: Gray or brown through the middle. banding: Hard steps where a blend was meant. dull: Flat, with little color or change. harsh: Glaring, clipped or too neon. dark: Mostly near black. light: Mostly near white. ugly: Passes through a color that spoils it. alike: Too close to another palette here. off: Doesn't fit the collection. form: Wrong style, steps or angle.

name: palette_titles
title: Title palettes
description: Write or replace the titles of palettes. A title is the palette page's own and search reads its words. A description is optional and kept when left out.

seed.description: A palette seed, as in its address: k and 8 to 49 more characters.

name: translations
title: Grabient's words in other languages
description: What Grabient's public collections and their tags still lack in one of the site's languages, with the English to translate from; or translations kept, beside their English: a random sample, or every one whose translator noted why a word or reference was adapted for the language. A collection whose English changed after it was translated is missing again. A tag lists the spellings the search already reads it by in that language's script.

kind.description: Collections (titles and descriptions) or tags. Default collections.

show.description: What is missing (the default), a sample of what is kept, or the kept translations with a note.

name: translations_save
title: Keep translations of Grabient's words
description: Keep translations of Grabient's public collections and their tags in one of the site's languages, replacing what that language had for them. A collection's entry carries the `source` translations gave with its English, so a translation of English that has changed since is refused. Each entry is checked: written in the language's script (a tag may stay as written), within the lengths, no line breaks and no em dash. The answer lists what was kept and what was refused, with why.

source.description: The `source` translations gave with its English.

note.description: Why a word or reference was adapted for this language, where it was: a meaning, a connotation or a name it has there that the English does not. One line in English, up to 300 characters.

tag.description: The tag, as Grabient writes it.

note.description: Why a word or reference was adapted for this language, where it was: a meaning, a connotation or a name it has there that the English does not. One line in English, up to 300 characters.

name: schedule
title: Schedule palettes and likes
description: Plan work for later, so the site keeps moving: the site applies what is due every ten minutes. A `collection` item adds palettes to a Grabient collection at its time, making the collection from the title given if no one has that slug. A `like` item has a persona like a palette at its time, which brings the palette into the public gallery and onto the home page as a reader's like does; it needs the palette in the gallery or in a public collection by then. `due` is a day (2026-10-05, applied at 14:00 UTC) or a moment (ISO 8601), up to 400 days ahead. Items spread over days and hours arrive as people would. `label` names the batch, to list or cancel it.

name: personas
title: The personas
description: The accounts scheduled likes are made with: stand-ins for readers, each with a taste, so the gallery's likes look like many people's. They never sign in and are shown nowhere. Lists them; `add` makes new ones or rewrites the taste of ones that exist. A persona's taste says which palettes its likes suit.

handle.description: 2 to 24 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens.

name: review_mark

description: Record what a review found, so work is not repeated: a verdict on a palette itself (how it looks), or on its fit when `collection` or `search` is given. One review stands per palette and subject; a new one replaces it. Reviews change nothing on the site.
